_what: The corridor sample set C126 checks a newly activated national GTFS feed against. Coordinate pairs and geography only — never feed content (AL-56).
_hardChecks: at least one DIRECT option is returned (BR-23.2: one route's stop sequence covers a halt near the origin BEFORE a halt near the destination)
every direct leg carries a shape, that shape decodes, and every point of it is inside the validator's Sri Lanka bounding box
the shape passes within shapeToleranceM of both ends of the corridor
_softChecks: expectRoutes is a HINT, and a miss is a warning rather than a failure. Route numbering is the feed's to state, not the platform's to require — AL-56 makes the file the authority, and a verify that failed because a provider renamed 138 to 138/1 would be asserting against the wrong thing. A miss is still printed loudly: on day-0 a corridor that returns routes but not the one everybody in Colombo rides is a question to ask the feed's provider.

_bbox._note: GtfsValidator.MinLat/MaxLat/MinLng/MaxLng — the same box BR-32.1 rejects stops outside of, so a shape and a stop are judged against one rule.

_shapeToleranceWhy: The halt radius is 400 m (BR-23.2), so the boarding halt is within 400 m of the requested point; a shape vertex is sampled along the road rather than at the halt, which adds a few hundred metres. 1200 m passes a real corridor and still fails a shape from the wrong side of the island by an order of magnitude.

corridors.label: Pettah → Kottawa (High Level Road)

from.name: Pettah / Bastian Mawatha bus stand, Colombo

corridors.why: The busiest bus corridor in the country and the one a Colombo passenger opens SCR-PA-009 for. If any corridor works, this one does.

corridors.label: Pettah → Moratuwa (Galle Road)

from.name: Pettah / Bastian Mawatha bus stand, Colombo

corridors.why: The second Colombo trunk, and a different geometry — coastal and nearly straight, where the High Level corridor bends. A router that scores by walk distance alone gets one of the two wrong.

corridors.label: Pettah → Negombo

from.name: Pettah / Bastian Mawatha bus stand, Colombo

corridors.why: Leaves the Colombo district, ~37 km. Catches a feed whose stop_times were truncated at a row limit: the far end of a long route is the first thing to go missing.

corridors.label: Kandy → Peradeniya
corridors.why: A short urban corridor outside the Western Province. This is the check that a feed is national rather than Colombo-only — the failure mode the retired corridor-first acquisition plan would have produced (AL-55/AL-56).

corridors.label: Galle → Matara
corridors.why: The Southern Province, and the southern extreme of the bounding box. A shape here is the strongest test of the bbox check: 5.9 °N is 0.2° from the validator's floor.

corridors.label: Pettah → Kandy

from.name: Pettah / Bastian Mawatha bus stand, Colombo

corridors.why: 115 km, the longest sample, and a rail corridor as well as a bus one — so it is where a train route legitimately appears among the direct options (Mode A covers bus and train, AL-18).
